Insight 1: "Emma Original and Emma Lite underperform in comparison to Emma Pro and other global competitor mattresses due to mattress cover perception and layfeel." Action 1: Engineers are prototyping new Original mattresses to upgrade stability of the Original line. Product brief for R&D was based on the PVT learnings. Timeline: June-September 2026 Action 2: Product design team is prototyping the new mattress covers. Covers are validated though an iterative testing in June-July. Timeline: June-September 2026

Insight 2: "Original Line consumers struggle to distinguish Original mattresses as the models are too visually similar to signal clear tiering or progression. Entry and mid-tier (Lite and Original) blur together, weakening perceived value." Action 1: Product design team is prototyping the new mattress covers (mentioned above). Timeline: June-September 2026 Action 2: CIX (in collaboration with CatMat; Creative; Global Brand) will test several portfolio configurations to identify the option that brings meaningful value difference between each of the tiers to consumer. Timeline (Concept test): mid June-mid August 2026

Insight 3: "Emma Original Pro is the strongest global performer winning on comfort-support balance as well as design." Action 1: Product brief for R&D took this into account making Original Pro an anchor for the upcoming product prototyping.

Insight 4: "A few countries (JP; DE) show a clear preference for a firmer profile - a mattress that feels firm in the core, supportive in the lower back and easy to move on." Action: Not implemented this quarter as we are prioritizing medium-soft cluster, but also integrated in the product brief.

Insight 5: "Consumers know what they want physically but lack the language to express it. Stated preference does not equal actual behavior." Action: CIX will be organizing workshops with country teams & global stakeholders (Global Brand; IM) to share relevant insights and ideate on action teams. Timeline: June-July 2026

"AU consumers rely on community-established signals (reviews, friend recommendations, platform ratings)" Action: Enroll in Trustpilot (¬10K/year) to address current low score (1.3) Timeline: June-July 2026

"AU consumers have a high need for detailed product specs, clear differentiation and stronger proof points" Action 1: Run full PDP audit using Luma's Source of Truth doc; identify incorrect, missing, or insufficiently detailed product info Timeline: June 2026 Action 2: Update copy from audit output and R&D input; pass through copywriting and Legal validation Timeline: July-August 2026

"JP consumer evidence requirements are one of the highest in the dataset - product claims must be proven" Action 1: Audit and update JP webshop comms Timeline: June-July 2026 Action 2: Collect scientific claims for use across webshop and paid media; update website Timeline: July 2026

"JP consumers respond to brands that signal safety, reliability, heritage, and institutional credibility" Action 1: Apply for local recognition and awards, including JIS certification Timeline: July-August 2026 Action 2: Showcase JIS recognition across webshop, paid media and CRM Timeline: July 2026

"JP over-indexes on testing as the quality-forming moment (34% vs. 29% global) -  highest of any market" Action: Better highlight offline presence on webshop; push 100-night trial across webshop and paid media Timeline: July 2026
"JP consumers are highly detail-oriented and expect thorough product information" Action: Run JP PDP audit (same workstream as AU, Stage 1 + Stage 2 above) Timeline: July-August 2026

"MX consumers are achievement-driven, socially visible and aspirational - they favour brands that signal success and market leadership" Action: Country brand strategy under review based on MX CIX results

Insight 1: "The burned-out consumer isn't looking for just another deal - they want permission to invest in themselves despite global uncertainty." Lean into self-investment framing Action: Implemented in BF script: "You can afford to dream"
Insight 2: "Life transitions drive the majority of mattress purchases." Touch on "new chapter" energy and nostalgia for good sleep Action: Implemented in BF TV script: "The details make the deal"

Planned additional research and working on a testing roadmap Australia: ~15-change roadmap across Sales Page, Home Page, Category Page, PDP. Defined testing roadmap

Insight 4: "Benefit-led storytelling outperforms spec-led copy" Actions: Japan: ~20-change roadmap across Sales Page, Home Page, Category Page, PDP. insights.desc: Insight 1: "Users think returning a mattress is a hassle and most don't consider it a real option leading them to delay purchase, buy from known brands, or visit physical stores instead" Action: AB test UK #58 Win. Return-focused USPs + return process modal on PDP +4.27% CVR +3.10% ATC +3.08% Begin Checkout +1.56% RPU -2.64% AOV Desktop: strong positive (+11.32% RPU). Mobile: funnel gains but AOV compression. Recommendation: roll out on desktop across all categories; revisit mobile before rolling out.
Insight 1: "Delivery window is too broad (3-10 days); exact date/time often only shared same-day" Action: Lead Time accuracy model daily-updated, live in 5 countries; the rest targeting June 2026
Insight 2: "Critical Emma and carrier communication conflict across touchpoints" Action: Order Status Page redesign - Phase 1 live; full rebuild targeting September 2026
Insight 3: "Order tracking is unreliable across most markets" Action: Order Status Page redesign - Phase 1 live; full rebuild targeting September 2026
Insight 4: "Return link is critical to customers and is missing from the confirmation email" Action: New Emma-owned Return Portal - targeting June 2026

Insight 5: "Returns pickup is unreliable and slow, causing high frustration levels and potential detraction" Action 1: New Emma-owned Return Portal - targeting June 2026 Action 2: Refunds speed & automation - targeting 4-day manual / 24-hour automated; target Q3 2026
Insight 1: "Customization is the #1 improvement lever - 51.8% want more control over pack composition"
Insight 2: "58% start with mattress intent; the bundle converts as an upgrade when savings are obvious"
Insight 3: "30-50% discount is the sweet spot - 55% need at least 30% off; deeper cuts hurt perceived quality"
Insight 4: "Detractors question quality and design more than cost - proof through reviews and certifications is the fix"

"The decision is mattress-led, then value-led: comfort/quality is #1, price/value is #2."
Action: Fix price trust (reduce discount confusion; show total cost): addresses unclear “actual price due to discounts.”

"Online sale is blocked by validation + choice overload: inability to try and too many choices drive hesitation."
Action 1: Callibrate the Product Finder (“Sleep Match”) + clear comparisons: reduce confusion on model differences; 
Action 2: Rationalize assortment into 3–5 core options: reduce choice overload using choice-architecture best practice.
Action 3: Bundle friction-removal services, delivery + assembly communicated prominently: aligns to top service demand and addresses online barriers.

"Independent tests are a major trust lever: independent awards/test results are strongly influential and often among the first things consumers look for."
Action: Leverage high awareness and influence of credible test brands (webshop, ads).
Action 2: Create a verifiable Trust Center around the products (tests, materials, warranty, proof):

"Buyers enter the Performance purchase journey through specific triggers"

Hypothesis:Leading acquisition messaging with the trigger that initiated the purchase journey will increase buyer self-identification, ad relevance and consideration compared to tech-led or premium-positioning communication.

Actions: Create separate creative routes for overheating, recovery / relief and differing household sleep needs.
A/B test trigger-led messaging against existing premium-sleep messaging across paid media and landing pages.

"Airgrid is a crucial differentiator for all buyers, but is valued for different reasons"

Hypothesis: Presenting AirGrid through distinct use-case narratives will increase feature relevance across a broader range of Performance evaluators and increase add-to-cart and conversion.

Action: Communicate AirGrid through three distinct use cases: relief from overheating, couple-sleep compatibility and differentiation as best product in the portfolio across marketing touchpoints.

"The same product appeals to two distinct buyer archetypes with different motivations, decision criteria and value perception."

Hypothesis: Tailoring messaging to the motivation of each archetype will increase message relevance, buyer self-identification and conversion compared to a single communication approach.

Actions: Build separate creative routes for the two buyer archetypes. For Relief Seekers, focus on recovery, relief, cooling and measurable improvement. For Thorough Upgraders, focus on long-term value, investment proof and the ability to try at home.

"Prior ownership creates a trust advantage that significantly reduces evaluation effort and increases confidence when considering higher-tier products within the Emma portfolio."

Hypothesis: Targeting existing Emma customers with upgrade-oriented messaging linked to evolving sleep needs, recovery goals and household changes will increase consideration and conversion into the Performance range.

Action: Launch a customer upgrade journey through CRM that re-engages existing Emma owners with messaging focused on improved sleep outcomes, recovery, temperature regulation, changing household needs and upgrading to the flagship mattress experience.

"Buyers use visual product hierarchy as a decision shortcut when navigating the portfolio."

H: Positioning Performance in the CP as the more premium tier, will increase conversion among a parcel of qualified buyers.

A: Introduce hierarchy cues on the category page that position Performance as the most premium product

"Buyers struggle to determine which Performance variant is right for them. Firmness and support are key topics that often remain unresolved until after purchase due to lack of information."

H: Providing directional guidance will lower return rates for Performance.

A: Improve firmness communication based on NPS feedback and support verbatims.
Improve the Performance 25 vs. Performance 28 vs. Performance 30 recommendation logic by linking body weight, support needs and desired feel to the recommended height variant.
Add a “Will this feel right for me?” like decision module on the Performance PDP linking body profile and sleeping preferences to expected firmness and feel.

"The 100-night-trial period is a crucial purchase driver and should be framed as a risk-transfer mechanism"

H: Reframing the trial period to explicitly address online purchase anxiety will increase conversion among first-time buyers without store access.

A: Increase visibility of the trial period near key decision moments and the CTA.
Reframe messaging around risk transfer, e.g. “Try Performance at home, worry-free. If it's not right for you, we'll take care of it.”

"Users increasingly adopt AI-assisted shopping behaviours. There is an opportunity to further refine the experience to reduce uncertainty and support decision-making"

H: Increasing the prominence of Product Finder and Chat AI throughout the journey and optimizing recommendation logic, will increase add-to-cart, improve product-selection accuracy and lower return rates.
Progressively adopting AI-assisted navigation in the webshop will make users arrive more seamlessly at product-fit and increase conversion.

A: Increase visibility of Product Finder and Chat AI early in the consideration journey.
Optimise recommendation logic to account for multiple needs and household dynamics.
Develop an AI-powered navigation layer that progressively shifts product discovery in the webshop from category browsing to need-based recommendation

"Price increase after size selection, immediately before basket addition, generate frustration, skepticism and friction at a critical stage of the conversion journey."

Requiring size selection before any price is displayed, or defaulting the displayed price to the most commonly purchased size, will increase add-to-cart.

Run an A/B test requiring size selection before displaying the final price, or defaulting the displayed price to the most common size.

"Airgrid is a crucial differentiator for all buyers, but is valued for different reasons"

H: Presenting AirGrid through distinct use-case narratives will increase feature relevance across a broader range of Performance evaluators and increase add-to-cart and conversion.

A: Communicate AirGrid through three distinct use cases: relief from overheating, couple-sleep compatibility and proof of premium differentiation across webshop touchpoints (Tags, Collection page, PDP).
